annotations.title: Find lots that match a list

description: Find the lots in one live Bucky city that match a list. Pass `city` or `geoDivisionId` with `thesis` (plain words), `criteria` (square feet, dollars), or both; or pass a saved `profileId`. Returns countOutcome (exact, partial, at_least, estimate, or unavailable), screeningRunId, and selected lots ranked largest first with a pass, fail, or not_available verdict per filter. totalMatches is a compatibility value and can be returned-page size when the total is unavailable. Report a not_available filter; never present the count as filtered by it. The execution preserves selection for optional candidate assessment; assessment candidate counts are separate from search totals. Returns candidates, counted suggestions and savedMatches. Candidate/suggestion criteria use the same square-foot boundary as the input, including canonical registry values and strategies. Present these alternatives before asking to save. Pass the selected criteria with save=true only after explicit approval, without re-reading the thesis. Each lot has `address` for getFeasibilitySnapshot and `parcelExternalId` for saveToProject. save=true saves the list (write scope) and returns a CSV link.

city.description: City as the user said it, e.g. "Laval" or "Bedford, MA". Omit when you pass geoDivisionId or profileId.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

criteria.description: Structured criteria. A field set here replaces the same field read from thesis.

branches.description: Alternative strategies; nested registry values stay in canonical units.

building_use.description: What the lot is used for today, read from the assessor's use code: office, mixed_use, retail, hospitality, industrial, multifamily, two_to_four_family, single_family, institutional, civic, religious, parking, vacant_land, other. "Commercial buildings, not houses or churches" is { any_of: ["office", "mixed_use", "retail"] } or { none_of: ["single_family", "two_to_four_family", "religious", "civic"] }.

contamination_risk.description: true: a gas station or auto-service business (repair, body shop, car wash) is mapped on the lot. { is: false } excludes those lots. A risk flag from OpenStreetMap and city business licences, not a site investigation: it misses former and unmapped businesses.

existing_coverage_pct.description: Building footprint area on the lot as a percentage of lot area, 0-100. An underbuilt screen is { max: 20 }. Footprints can be years old: check the city honesty note.

existing_use_class.description: What stands on the lot: place_of_worship (church, temple, mosque, synagogue…), fuel_station, auto_service (repair, body, car wash), auto_sales (car dealer), else vacant, surface_parking or built. "Vacant lots or surface parking" is { any_of: ["vacant", "surface_parking"] }; "gas stations" is { any_of: ["fuel_station"] }; "church sites" is { any_of: ["place_of_worship"] }. Vacant means no building over 20 m² in any footprint source and no assessed building worth over 20% of the land. Québec lots without footprints use the assessment roll land-use code (CUBF 9100 = vacant). A mapped business on the lot wins over the footprint class. Fuel and auto-service sites are a contamination risk flag, not a site investigation.

exterior_material.description: The assessor's primary exterior wall as a family: masonry, wood, siding, stucco, concrete, metal, glass, other. "Brick buildings" is { any_of: ["masonry"] }.

frequent_transit_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest frequent bus stop or rapid-transit station.

hydrant_distance.description: Metres from the lot line to the nearest fire hydrant.

improvement_land_ratio.description: Building (improvement) value divided by land value, assessed or appraised, as a ratio: 0.25 = the building is worth a quarter of the land. A teardown screen is { max: 0.25 }.

ocp_above_zoning.description: true: the lot's Official Community Plan designation allows more housing than its current zone (both ranked 1 rural, 2 low density, 3 medium density, 4 high density or mixed-use centre): a rezoning candidate. { is: false } keeps lots where both are ranked and the OCP is not higher. Lots with an unranked zone or designation, no zone, or no designation match neither. A planning signal: a rezoning consistent with the OCP is more likely to be supported, but this is not a rezoning approval or the density zoning permits today.

owner_class.description: Owner class of the titled parcels on the lot, from ParcelMap BC owner type: private, municipal, provincial, federal, crown_agency, mixed_ownership (as the source states), unclassified, and public (any of municipal, provincial, federal, crown_agency). A lot with parcels of several classes holds all of them, so none_of ["public"] also drops a lot that is partly public and any_of ["private"] keeps it. "Not public land" is { none_of: ["public"] }, which keeps lots whose owner class is unknown; any_of drops them. "Private" is the registered owner type, not a title search.

ownership_form.description: Ownership form: fee_simple (land title), strata_condo, co_op, leasehold, mixed. "Land title only" is { none_of: ["strata_condo", "co_op", "leasehold", "mixed"] }, which keeps lots whose form is unknown; any_of drops them.

place_of_worship.description: true: a church, temple, mosque, synagogue or other place of worship is mapped on the lot (OpenStreetMap, city heritage registers). { is: false } excludes those lots. Same lots as existing_use_class place_of_worship.

register_status.description: Historic register status: individually_listed, contributing, non_contributing, in_district (inside a register district, building not yet mapped), not_listed. "On the register" is { any_of: ["individually_listed", "contributing"] }. Register status is a research lead, not tax-credit eligibility. The federal 20% credit needs a certified historic structure; building age alone qualifies for nothing (the 10% pre-1936 credit was repealed in 2017).

stories.description: Above-grade stories: the assessor count where recorded (half stories are decimals, 1.5), otherwise estimated from building height at 3 m per storey. "1-2 story" is { max: 2 }.

street.description: Street names as the lot address carries them, upper case with the suffix abbreviated: "STATE ST", "BANK ST". { any_of: [...] } keeps lots on those streets. Matches the lot's address, not every street it touches: a corner lot counts once.

subdivision_yield.description: Lot area divided by the zone's minimum lot area: how many minimum-size lots the parcel could hold by area. "Could be subdivided" is { min: 2 }; "into 3 lots" is { min: 3 }. Ignores frontage, streets and lot shape: a candidate, not a subdivision approval.

titled_unit_count.description: Titled units on the parcel: 1 for a land-title lot, the strata unit count otherwise.

tract_rent_2br.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey average monthly rent for a 2-bedroom purpose-built rental unit in the census tract holding the lot centre, CAD, inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

tract_rental_vacancy.description: CMHC Rental Market Survey vacancy rate, all bedroom types, purpose-built rental, in the census tract holding the lot centre, percent (1.5 = 1.5%), inclusive bounds. Lots in tracts CMHC does not publish never match.

typology.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Exact typology IDs; sector-only lots do not match.

use_sector.description: Current site use from site_typologies, not what can be built. Sector IDs; includes sector-only assignments.

year_built.description: Year the main building was built, inclusive bounds.

zone_family.description: The zone's dominant use: residential, mixed, commercial, industrial, public, recreation, agricultural, forest. "Zoned residential or mixed" is { any_of: ["residential", "mixed"] }. Québec zones read the zone letter (H, M, C, I, P/U, R, A, F); other zones a family classified from the zone name and purpose. The family names the dominant use; the bylaw still decides which uses are permitted.

maxAssessed.description: Highest assessed total value, in dollars.

minAssessed.description: Lowest assessed total value, in dollars.

minHomes.description: Homes allowed, at least N. A zone-level estimate.

namedAreaIds.description: Submarket (named area) ids. Use `thesis` to match submarkets by name.

overlayExcludeKinds.description: Overlay kinds a lot must not overlap. A lot passes only if it was evaluated for every excluded kind; an unevaluated kind is reported not_available.

overlayKinds.description: Overlay kinds a lot must overlap by at least 1 m². A kind the city has not evaluated is reported not_available, never applied.

geoDivisionId.description: Division id, from an earlier screenLots or cityInventory result.

hygiene.description: Default true. Ad-hoc lists leave out public owners (owner_class), cap lot size at 5 acres and ignore assessed values under $100,000 where the city stores them, unless criteria set the same field. Each default is named in notes. false skips them. Ignored with profileId: a saved list runs as saved.

limit.description: Lots to return. Default 10. countOutcome states whether the total is exact, partial, at_least (a lower bound), estimate (about), or unavailable.

profileId.description: Saved list id. Runs the saved city and criteria. Do not combine with city, thesis, or criteria.

save.description: true saves the list to the account. Default false. Search execution history is recorded.

thesis.description: The list in plain words, e.g. "industrial lots over half an acre outside the floodplain".
